items.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And he recorded in the early 60s Sam Cooke and people like that

ctx.x: I bet you were holding your breath, right?

You know there’s a great engineer/producer out in LA named Al Schmidt who is in his late 80s now. And I think he won a Grammy two years ago. He started out when he was a kid in New York. He’s one of the masters of all time. And he recorded in the early 60s Sam Cooke and people like that, up through Norah Jones. He’s still winning Grammys. He’s won I think 20, 22 Grammys. And Al told me one time, when I had one of those big dates, a roomful of players, one of the words of wisdom, “Just don’t let them see you…

when there was 35 people sitting out there and the tape machine would break right before the session, and we’d have to sit there for an hour. You’re looking at your watch and they’re looking at their watches. Because they know they’re only there for three hours; maybe two sessions, six hours. And you’ve got to get it. And the tape machine broke one time and we wasted an hour while they fixed that. The studio is not going to pay for those musicians. But we had to cram into two hours what we would have done in…
